findings.title: Ambiguity regex misses connection drops after the body is sent
findings.body: `ambiguousUploadError` only matches HTTP 5xx/408 and timeout wording. If the connection is reset or closed after gh has sent the 16 MB body (for example `connection reset by peer`, `unexpected EOF`, or `read: connection reset`), the request may have been stored, but stderr matches none of the patterns. That case falls through to line 22 and is shown as a definite failure with a retry path. A retry then creates the duplicate this PR is trying to prevent. Treat a failure after the body was written, other than a definite HTTP 4xx response, as unconfirmed. Alternatively, extend the pattern to cover reset/EOF/broken-pipe errors. I did not read gh's exact stderr text for these errors, so this is not confirmed.

findings.title: Timeout assertion uses an arbitrary threshold and only runs in the unconfirmed cases
findings.body: `toBeGreaterThan(34_000)` passes for any value above 34 s. It does not pin the 120 s upload timeout, and it does not check that GET calls such as `findArtifactIssues` keep 30 s, which is the other half of the `body ? 120_000 : 30_000` change. Assert `toBe(120_000)` on the POST. Add a lookup test that asserts 30_000.

contracts.action: Publish artifact: a gh timeout or ambiguous 5xx now resolves as {status:'unconfirmed'} with the issue URL instead of rejecting
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-change path: ghApi rejected every error with stderr or a generic message, and the dialog showed an alert with the mutation still retryable.
contracts.before_after: Before: any failure produced add.error and the form stayed, so one click retried. After: failures with error.killed or matching stderr become UploadUnconfirmed (line 21) and publishIssueArtifact maps them to a result (line 60). Definite errors still throw (line 22). Connection resets that are not 5xx/408/timeout still throw, so retry stays one click away (see finding).
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog title becomes 'Upload unconfirmed' with a check-before-retry notice, an Open issue button and a Back button. Back resets the mutation to the form.
contracts.failure_mode: Only the connection-drop case above is misclassified. gh not installed or not signed in has killed=false and empty or specific stderr, so it gives the generic or stderr alert.

contracts.action: Wait bound for the upload: the POST timeout rises from 30 s to 120 s
contracts.equivalent_path: The same ghApi path with the 30 s timeout used by the GET lookups (findArtifactIssues).
contracts.before_after: The execFile timeout bounds only the gh child process, and now only for body requests. The IPC handler first awaits ensureShellEnv() (frontend/src/main.ts:3890-3895). The renderer awaits readContent() before the call (GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx:58). Neither has its own limit here, and both were already there before this PR. There is exactly one sequential gh call, so the total is about 120 s plus those two awaits.
contracts.visible_effect: For up to about 2 minutes the dialog cannot be closed. The close button is hidden and onOpenChange ignores close while add.isPending (GitHubIssueArtifactDialog.tsx:91-92), and the button reads 'Adding…'. After 120 s the user sees the unconfirmed state.
contracts.failure_mode: When the timeout kills gh, the result is 'unconfirmed', which is visible. If ensureShellEnv or readContent never settles, the dialog stays locked, as it did before.

contracts.action: Dialog success view handles status 'unconfirmed' and keeps a destination captured at mutation time
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous success view: a single View button that opened add.data, which was a string.
contracts.before_after: Before, the description rebuilt the destination from live `repo` and `selected`. Now `destination` is stored in the mutation result (line 59), so it cannot drift. The Back button calls add.reset() (line 103), which returns to the form with repo and selected intact. The user can resubmit manually after the warning. openExternal receives add.data.url, which in the unconfirmed case is built from the validated repository and the issue number (main/github-issue-artifact.ts:60).
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the unconfirmed title, role=status guidance, and Back and Open issue buttons. The test asserts the status text, openExternal(url), Back re-enabling the Add button, and publish called once.
contracts.failure_mode: Not applicable. The only async call (publish) rejecting is handled by the existing add.error alert.

contracts.action: Client-side 16,777,215-byte limit check on the UTF-8 body before invoking gh
contracts.equivalent_path: Other validations in publishIssueArtifact (lines 49-52) throw plain English Error messages before gh runs.
contracts.before_after: Before, an oversized file was sent and GitHub rejected it, or it timed out. Now the check throws before any process is started, and the test asserts exec is not called.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog shows the English error message in the add.error alert, like the other main-process validation errors.
contracts.failure_mode: The error is visible. The message is not localized, but the neighbouring validation messages are English as well.

summary: The change is sound and well covered by tests. It returns an `unconfirmed` result for ambiguous upload failures and shows a check-before-retry state. It also adds a UTF-8 size guard and 10 locale strings. I found two minor points. The ambiguity regex does not cover connection reset or EOF after the body is sent, so a one-click retry can still duplicate the artifact in that case. The timeout test asserts a loose `> 34_000` bound instead of the 120 s value.
